Marco García Es un profesional con grado de Maestro especializado en el desarrollo de videojuegos y efectos visuales. Su formación académica incluye una licenciatura en Programación de Videojuegos por SAE Institute México, una doble titulación en Gestión Universitaria por parte de la Universidad Anáhuac y la Universidad de Alcalá, así como dos maestrías: un Máster en Efectos Visuales por Voxel School y un Máster en Desarrollo de Videojuegos por la Universidad de La Laguna.

Con más de 8 años de experiencia docente a nivel universitario y 7 años en la industria de los videojuegos, Marco ha desempeñado una variedad de roles que abarcan desde artista técnico en Game Coder Studios hasta supervisor académico y docente. Actualmente, es Lead Developer en el estudio alemán Players Journey, donde lidera proyectos innovadores en el ámbito de los videojuegos.

Se especializa en el desarrollo de juegos y aplicaciones interactivas en realidad virtual mixta y plataformas móviles, con una sólida experiencia en herramientas como Unity (8 años) y Unreal Engine (5 años). A lo largo de su carrera, ha participado en la creación de videos musicales y en la producción virtual para televisión en México y España, utilizando Unreal Engine para proyectos inmersivos y de alto impacto visual. Nagida is a design researcher specialising in immersive experiences. She is a PhD candidate with UNSW Art and Design, supported through a scholarship with CSIRO’s Data61. Her research investigates embodied sensemaking for researchers interacting with ocean and wildfire visualisations in real-time, 3D environments. Here, she explores multisensory approaches to bring these visualisations to life.
Nagida applies her research through UNSW iCinema’s ARC Laureate iFire project, where she worked as an Interaction Designer before commencing her PhD. iFire is an immersive environment able to visualise extreme wildfire behaviour. Nagida is working closely with wildfire researchers and firefighters to understand fire dynamics and translate this into her designs. She is also embedded in CSIRO’s Data61 Ocean Explorer project. Here, she is working with oceanographers to explore the aesthetic characteristics of ocean current models through haptics.
Nagida graduated from UNSW’s Master of Visualisation, Simulation and Immersive Design in 2021 with Excellence. She was the recipient of the UNSW Art and Design Dean’s List Award in 2020 and 2021. Nagida has a strong interest in narrative and visual storytelling, having studied a diploma in cinematography at AFTRS and journalism at UTS in her undergraduate years. Before training as a designer, Nagida worked and volunteered as a climate, LGBTQIA+ and workplace rights digital storyteller and community organiser. She draws on these values and skills in her design process, emphasising participatory and more-than-human methodologies to grapple with the climate crisis.
Nagida is a sessional academic teaching in the immersive design program at UNSW Art and Design.

employment_edges.excerpt: Smit Desai sm.desai@northeastern.edu chainortheastern.net Lab: CHAI Lab (Conversational Human-AI Interactions Lab) Department: Art + Design Center or Institute Affiliation: Communication Studies, Khoury College of Computer Science Communication Studies, Khoury College of Computer ScienceCommunication Studies, Khoury College of Computer Science Position Description: The Conversational Human-AI Interactions (CHAI) Lab welcomes students with diverse disciplinary and technical backgrounds who share an interest in designing and studying human-centered AI systems. We are particularly interested in students with expertise in: -Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), Human Factors, and Communication Studies - skills in qualitative/ quantitative/ mixed-methods research, participatory/co-design, ethnography, and experimental design. -Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, and Data Science - strong programming experience (e.g., Python, web backends), familiarity with machine learning and large language models (LLMs), conversational AI toolkits, and data analysis. -Design and Creative Disciplines - skills in interaction design, prototyping (low- and high- fidelity), and information visualization. -Students with hybrid skill sets across design, computing, and human-AI communication are especially encouraged to apply. Looking ahead, the lab is expanding into: -Healthcare applications of conversational AI (e.g., supporting crisis or serious illness communication). -AI for aging and accessibility (e.g., reminiscence technologies, voice-based companions). -Personalization and personality in LLM-based agents (e.g., tailoring conversational style, affect, or personality to user needs). -Responsible and explainable AI (e.g., transparency, ethics, and policy implications of human-AI collaboration). INTERDISCIPLINARY DESIGN AND MEDIA PHD RECRUITING FACULTY - FALL 2026 Students with interests or expertise in these domains will find rich opportunities to shape the lab’s trajectory. Research Expectations: During their first two years, research assistants (RAs) in CHAI Lab are expected to contribute to funded projects through activities such as: -Designing and running user studies with patients, older adults, or everyday users. -Conducting interviews, surveys, and qualitative/quantitative data analysis. -Prototyping and developing conversational interfaces (voice and chat-based) using LLMs and related technologies. -Assisting with IRB applications, study logistics, and cross-institution collaborations. Develop technical and methodological skills, including: -Building and iterating on research prototypes/ systems. -Applying human-centered AI design principles. -Using established measures (e.g., trust, usability, workload) to evaluate conversational systems. Engage in dissemination, including: -Drafting and revising papers for venues such as ACM CHI, CSCW, and CUI. -Presenting findings at lab meetings, conferences, and workshops. By the end of their second year, students will have contributed substantially to one or more ongoing projects, developed a clear methodological toolkit, and begun defining their own independent research trajectory within the lab’s themes of personalization, collaboration, and support in conversational AI. Research Interests: Human-Computer Interaction, Conversational AI, Large Language Models INTERDISCIPLINARY DESIGN AND MEDIA PHD RECRUITING FACULTY - FALL 2026

employment_edges.excerpt: Andy Nealen – Andy Nealen is an Associate Professor of Cinematic Arts and Computer Science in the Interactive Media & Games Division at the USC School of Cinematic Arts and the Department of Computer Science at USC Viterbi. He teaches and researches in Game Design, Artificial Intelligence, Computer Graphics, and Game Engineering. Andy's work seeks to increase the accessibility of computer-based tools across a variety of application environments, drawing upon minimalist principles he first encountered while obtaining his Dipl.-Ing. in Architecture and Structural Engineering from TU Darmstadt. In particular, his research leverages and extends our understanding of how humans perceive shape, motion, and color. This focus on minimal and accessible designs for complex systems is evidenced in the Apple-Design-Award-winning game Osmos, as well as in his Sketch-Based Modeling, Game-Space Exploration, and Game Heuristics research. Andy received his PhD in Computer Science from TU Berlin, is a regular speaker at international game and computer graphics conferences, and is a regular contributor to ACM SIGGRAPH.

Dr. Xiaomeng Wu is an associate Professor in Graduate School of Education and the Lab of Learning Sciences.  She was once a visiting scholar in Berlin Freie University.
Her research interests are teaching and learning in school with ICT, online learning, information literacy education for youth, PBL, teacher learning and professional development. She published many research papers and a monograph named Understanding the Teachers in Educational Change. She has served as the editor-in-chief and author of books such as "Conducting Learning Science Research: A Handbook for Teachers".
In addition to academic research she has collaborated with Intel, Chinese Association of Science and Technology (CAST) and ICT companies as a consultant, trainer and project collaborator.

### Associate Professor

TreaAndrea M. Russworm, Ph.D. - Dr. Russworm is the Microsoft Endowed Chair and a Professor in the Interactive Media & Games Division at the University of Southern California. She is also the founder of Radical Play (a games-based public humanities initiative and after school program), and she has been a professor and Associate Dean of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion at UMass Amherst. A prolific author and editor, Russworm is a Series Editor of Power Play: Games, Politics, Culture (Duke University Press). She is the author or editor of three books: Blackness is Burning; Gaming Representation; and Theorizing Tyler Perry. With research expertise in digital culture, video games, and popular African American media, Professor Russworm’s scholarship and interviews have also been shared on CNN, The History Channel, Turner Classic Movies, in podcasts, and on streaming platforms like Twitch. She is a video game Hall of Fame voter, and she is currently writing a new monograph on The Sims and a book on race and the politics of play.

Dr. Ran Wei is an Assistant Professor at the Graduate School of Education, Peking University. Her research program, situated at the intersection of developmental psychology, neuroscience, linguistics, and early childhood education, adopts an interdisciplinary and cross-cultural approach. It aims to understand how early language and cognitive development unfolds in diverse societies, cultures, and languages. Her present research endeavors include: 1) elucidating the neural networks that support young children's language and executive function development; 2) examining how factors in the home environment, particularly caregiver communicative input and beliefs, foster language and executive function development, especially amidst early adversity and in under-resourced settings; and 3) creating effective AI-assisted interventions to support parents from varied socioeconomic backgrounds in nurturing their children's learning and development. Dr. Wei utilizes a diverse array of methods and approaches, including eye-tracking, EEG, behavioral experiments, linguistic analysis of verbal and nonverbal interactions, and LENA. She is dedicated to transforming research findings into culturally attuned insights for parents, educators, and the broader community.

Dr Steph Craig is a nurse academic and researcher with a specialist focus on the care of older people and interdisciplinary healthcare education. Her research is grounded in long-term conditions and complex care needs, with particular expertise in dementia, Parkinson’s disease, stroke, heart failure, delirium, and diabetes care.
She is widely published in these areas and is particularly committed to collaborative research with under-served and underrepresented populations through accelerated co-design methodologies.
Dr Craig has a strong interest in digital education, including the design, development, and evaluation of educational resources and serious games for healthcare professionals. Methodologically, she is highly experienced in realist evaluation and realist synthesis, as well as mixed methods research, grounded theory, and ethnography. She is open to supervising students across these domains.

"" - Pablo Hurtado-Sorto

EMAIL: pablo23@illinois.edu ONLINE: visit Pablo Hurtado-Sorto's portfolio site†pablohurtado.artstation.com and LinkedIn profile†www.linkedin.com .
Pablo Hurtado‑Sorto is a 3D Character Artist with over 13 years of experience in the video game industry. He began his career as an Associate Artist at Deadpanic Studios, contributing to the development of Orcs Must Die Unchained!. He then worked as a contract artist at NetherRealm Studios, where he helped bring to life Injustice: Gods Among Us Mobile and Mortal Kombat X Mobile.
Following that, Pablo joined EA Tiburon, where he spent several years working on the Madden NFL franchise—from Madden 17 through Madden 23—and played a key role in the development of The Yard avatar system and other character customization features. Today, Pablo works as a freelance character artist, collaborating with indie studios and clients around the world.
His recent projects include Avatar work for Sparq Games and his ongoing role as Senior Character Artist on an unannounced Unreal Engine 5-based action-adventure title in development at Bloxneo. Alongside his production work, Pablo shares his industry knowledge as an adjunct instructor at the University of Illinois and as a Class Supervisor at Think Tank Training Centre, where he mentors aspiring 3D artists preparing to enter the professional field.
He studied Game Design and Production at the International Academy of Design and Technology in Chicago, which laid the foundation for his career in games Companies I have worked with: EA Tiburon, NetherRealm Studios, Bloxneo, Dead panic Studios, and Think Tank training Centre.
COURSES:

  * GSD 522 Tools & Techniques: Contemporary Techniques for 3D Art in Games

Um eine*n Promotionsbetreuer*in an der TH Köln zu finden, empfehlen wir Ihnen, zunächst ein Exposé (Kurzbeschreibung Ihres Vorhabens) zu Ihrer Promotionsidee zu verfassen. Auf den Webseiten der TH Köln sind die Professor*innen aller Fakultäten aufgeführt. Suchen Sie nach einer Person, die fachlich zu Ihrem Forschungsvorhaben passt und schreiben oder sprechen Sie diese mit Ihrem Exposé an.
Professor*innen der TH Köln finden Sie folgendermaßen: Gehen Sie auf die TH Köln-Startseite, wählen Sie unter "Hochschule" > "Fakultäten" die passende Fakultät aus. Auf jeder Fakultätsseite finden Sie links eine Seite "Personen (an der Fakultät)". Auf dieser können Sie unter "Status" nach "Professorinnen und Professoren" filtern.
TH Köln Startseite
+
Wie finde ich eine*n Betreuer*in an einer Hochschule mit Promotionsrecht in Deutschland oder im Ausland?
Um eine*n Promotionsbetreuer*in an einer Hochschule mit Promotionsrecht zu finden, empfehlen wir Ihnen, zunächst ein Exposé (Kurzbeschreibung Ihres Vorhabens) zu Ihrer Promotionsidee zu verfassen. Suchen Sie nach Hochschulen mit Promotionsrecht, die in Ihrem Bereich einen passenden Forschungsschwerpunkt anbieten. Anschließend kontaktieren Sie die Person, die fachlich zu Ihrem Forschungsvorhaben passt und klären, ob der*die Wissenschaftler*in Interesse daran hat, Ihre Promotion zu betreuen. Wenn Sie bereits eine*n Betreuer*in an der TH Köln haben, fragen Sie diese*n nach geeigneten Kolleg*innen, die die kooperative Promotion an einer Hochschule mit Promotionsrecht betreuen könnten.
+
Mit welchen Hochschulen sind Kooperationen möglich?
Grundsätzlich sind Kooperationen mit jeder promotionsberechtigten Hochschule weltweit möglich.
Eine Vermittlung zu einer Hochschule, über die das kooperative Promotionsverfahren abgewickelt werden kann, ist seitens der Verwaltung der TH Köln nicht möglich. Einige Professor*innen der TH Köln haben allerdings bereits guten Kontakt zu Kolleg*innen an Hochschulen mit Promotionsrecht, mit denen sie im besten Fall sogar bereits gemeinsam eine Promotion betreut haben.
Natürlich können Sie auch auf eigene Kontakte oder Netzwerke zurückgreifen, um die passende Hochschule mit Promotionsrecht für eine kooperative Promotion zu finden.
+

Promotion am PK NRW
Seit dem Promotionskolleg für angewandte Forschung in Nordrhein-Westfalen (PK NRW) im Herbst 2022 das Promotionsrecht verliehen wurde, gibt es außerdem die Möglichkeit, ein Promotionsvorhaben in einem strukturierten Promotionsprogramm am PK NRW zu realisieren. In diesem Fall führen die Promovierenden ihre Promotion an der TH Köln durch und werden von einem Betreuungsteam aus Mitgliedern des PK NRW betreut. Der Doktortitel wird hier vom PK NRW verliehen.
Kooperative Promotion
Eine kooperative Individualpromotion ist aktuell an der TH Köln noch der häufigste Weg, den Promovierende verfolgen. Hier nehmen zukünftige Promovierende individuell Kontakt zu einer*m Professor*in auf (sowohl an der TH Köln als auch an einer Hochschule mit Promotionsrecht) und verfassen ihre Dissertation selbstorganisiert und unabhängig von einem festgelegten Programm.
Zur Förderung des wissenschaftlichen Nachwuchses hat die TH Köln neben der Individualpromotion als Betreuungsstruktur auf Fakultätsebene derzeit Promotionskolloquien und Promotionsprogramme etabliert. Zudem ist die TH Köln im Rahmen einer strukturierten Promovierendenausbildung an einigen öffentlich geförderten Promotionskollegs beteiligt.

About Programme

Aims & Characteristics

**Programme Aims**

This programme is aimed at developing designer-researchers who can conduct practice-based design research and who have a good understanding of how to extend their professional practice. Our students can make a substantial contribution to society through the knowledge they have gained and can offer novel solutions to societal problems by accessing the potential that has previously lain dormant within them.

The programme strongly encourages the development of analytical capabilities, in addition to design skills, by instructing students in a variety of research approaches, and promotes an attitude of collaboration.

**Characteristics**

*   Practice-based research: Advancing various design research directions for societal development and system changes.

*   Trans-disciplinary: The application of research knowledge related to design across a wide range of disciplinary boundaries, which can influence the design industry and communities of the future.

*   A flexible programme structure and outcome: Customisable to meet the ever-changing demands of the market and to provide students with extensive design knowledge.

Recognition & Prospects

Students will graduate with a Doctorate of Design (DDes) after successfully completing all subjects (as listed in the curriculum) and a thesis, and can then use the title ‘Dr’.

routes.name: UC Designing for Extremes: Immersive VR Simulation for Embodied Technology Design in Antarctic Fieldwork

evidence.excerpt: Per annum: Stipend of $32,650 plus PhD tuition fees. The project also has up to $5,000 available for research expenses across the duration of the degree.

This PhD project will use immersive Virtual Reality (VR) to simulate sensory and physical constraints of Antarctic fieldwork, letting designers experience and address embodied demands directly, without the cost or risk of testing prototypes in the field.

Final date for receiving applications
27 October 2026
If English is not your first language, you are also required to meet UC's Postgraduate language requirements.
PhD students must contact a potential supervisor before applying.
